 How to write to us...02     -
 Bob Ringsell.........03    05
 Alan Rutherford......08     -

      HOW TO WRITE TO OUTLET
      ----------------------
Letters are accepted  in  almost
any form for publication in our
OUTLETTERS: BASIC PRINT or  DATA
statements, handwritten or typed
pages, a simple  JOTTER  program
is provided in Issue 2(Opus #4);
mailbox messages via Prestel No.
014703943 but the easiest for us
to edit are Tasword 2 files with
the right-hand margin set at 32.

Please state if there should  be
parts of your letter you do  not
wish published but we always use
our discretion  anyway.  Letters
may also be edited  for  clarity
and length... Please ask if  you
welcome  direct   correspondence
from other OUTLET readers and we
will publish your full address.

From Bob Ringsell, H/Hempstead

Dear Ron & Brian,

Please tell me what I am doing
wrong. In OUTLET No. 12 the prog
OUTDEX will not update, i.e. I
load OUTDEX from No.12 then load
data from No.13 by pressing L
then I replace No.12 back in the
disc drive and press U(to reSAVE
the program). All is O.K. when
displayed to the screen straight
away but the next time I load
No. 12 so I can update say No.14
it has not saved No. 13, i.e. it
does not save the new data.

I would like to use the program
EXPENSHEET, Issue No.12 but when
I try to change line No.9170

from say, set at 5 to 6 it makes
no difference and still only
accepts a max off `99.99.

Please help.

Yours sincerely,

Bob Ringsell

To Bob Ringsell from Brian

Ron has already replied to you
directly re: OUTDEX but just to
clarify: when OUTDEX updates
itself with new data it saves as
"OUTDEX"  whereas it is saved as
"out" in the original OUTLET
Issue 12.I should have made this
clearer in the first place. My
intention was for users to make
a separate, working copy which
is then loaded separately from
the issue by loading "OUTDEX"
directly leaving the original as
a back-up. When you used the
"update" option it (presumably)
DID save correctly (as "OUTDEX")
but when you re-loaded it next
month from the CONTENTS page you
were actually loading "out" -the


original which was unchanged!If,
in future,you always load OUTDEX
directly it should be alright.

I did not think that anyone
would need to input single items
of more than `99.99 on their
monthly expense sheet! This can
be corrected however,as follows:

As you did, BREAK in and alter
the 2nd value at line 9170 from
5 to 6.[the number of characters
in 999.99 (pounds) ]

Reduce the LET MXL=26 to 25 in
line 9110 (This will limit the
maximum length of item descript-
ion but stops the display and
print-out getting badly out of
line).

Alter: IF VAL L$ >= CODE "d" in
line 1136 to: IF VAL L$ >= 1000.
(Enabling you to input items
with a value up to `999.99!)

Finally, an adjustment near the
end of a long line at 1110 so
cursor through patiently!...

... IF NOT LEN L$ OR LEN L$ > O5
should be altered to ... O6

I have tested it briefly and it
seems alright but don't hesitate
to write again if any further
problem develops.

I use EXPENSHEET regularly (with
more modest amounts!) and it
works like a dream.
                        - Brian

From Michael Williams

Dear Ron and Brian,

In OUTLET #12, the JACKSOFT INFO
file prints out on my CANON
PW-1080 (EPSON COMPATIBLE)
printer at 32 chars/line in the
middle of the page with double
line spacing. I would prefer
this long file to be printed out
at 80 chars/line with SINGLE
line spacing and I would be glad
if you could tell me how to
achieve this. (Spectrum 128 &
DISCIPLE with GDOS 3d)

John Luby doesn't need to
apologise. It's not pompous to
deplore spelling mistakes
(OUTLETTERS #16), even though he


mis-spells "calendar" in his own
program (CAL-PLAN) in the same
issue of OUTLET! Inaccuracies in
programming will often have dire
effects.Inaccuracies in spelling
can have similar effects on
one's readers. It hurts to have
my internal "line editor" scream
REJECT! REJECT! whenever it
meets a spelling mistake - for
example, when IT'S is used
wrongly for ITS. (See EDITORIAL
#16 "it's purpose")

Why should readers have to
grapple with self-indulgent or
ignorant idiosyncracies which
can only irritate, at best, or
at worst, hinder understanding?
Pompous though it might sound
care and precision are simply a
form of courtesy.

It always surprises me to find
how often mis-spellings and bad
grammar occur on computer
bulletin boards, for example. I
would have thought that the type
of mind which, presumably,
enjoys the meticulous demands of
programming would also feel the
need to spell and write
accurately. Maybe it's only a
minority who enjoy programming.

I'm glad to say that OUTLET
usually offends less than other
publications in this respect. In
fact, I believe I remember
reading a review of yours where
some program was strongly
criticised for being amateurish
and full of spelling mistakes,
among other things.

I was interested to read your
comments on "the mysterious
secret society of INDUG" (OUTLET
#16). I have been a member since
I bought my DISCIPLE in May
1987. There is a very good
monthly magazine called FORMAT
which I look forward to almost
as much as I do to OUTLET (and
BETA BASIC NEWSLETTER).

All DISCIPLE-buyers are offered
a free introductory issue of
FORMAT and have the opportunity
to take out a subscription.

It's true that the editor is
rather elusive. A couple of my
letters have gone unanswered,
orders have been unfulfilled and
a longstanding cheque has not
yet been presented.

Thank you both for a unique and
excellent publication. It
deserves a far larger readership
than the present couple of
hundred. I will certainly
continue to sing its praises to
my Spectrum-owning friends and
on Micronet. Incidentally, I
heard several people expressing
interest in OUTLET at the recent
Microfair and wondering why you
weren't represented there. In my
opinion, if many more exhibitors
abandon the MF it won't be worth
continuing. It's already
degenerated into a pretty feeble
event.

Best wishes for a happy and
relaxing Xmas and for a success-
ful 1989.
                Michael Williams

To Michael Williams from Brian

I regret that our present print
routine cannot provide 80 column
print-outs.I'm reviewing all the
print routines but this may take
a while.Mike Haine is developing
a multi-column "newspaper-style"
routine for us which we hope to
include in a future issue either
as a stand-alone program or to
replace our present system.

Meanwhile, in response to your
request, I've written a program
to give 80 column format and I
will squeeze it in this issue
somehow.I may have to put some
other program back a month. The
program is called COL80.It works
better than I'd hoped although

some text, like headings, are
printed oddly because they have
been spaced out to display on
screen. Hope it suffices for the
time being.

I take full responsibility for
any spelling or grammatical
errors in OUTLET. All text is
checked repeatedly as carefully
as I know how so forgive me if a
mistake gets overlooked.

"elusive", you say! I have in
front of me a copy of our letter
to INDUG dated 18th February,
1988 to "...ask if we might join
INDUG" (enclosing a free copy of
OUTLET) and our letter of 13th
May in similar vein enclosing
another free copy of OUTLET...

and our 3rd letter of 5th August
very politely asking "...if we
might join the user group" and
AGAIN enclosing a free disk!

We were not writing letters of
complaint, begging for money or
making pointless lengthy, and
time-wasting comments - we were
simply asking to join the group!
We have not received any reply
whatsoever - not even a note or
a leaflet on "how to join". In
fairness, we've heard elsewhere
that Bob Brenchley wanted to
phone Ron but couldn't find the
telephone number! With Ron runn-
ing CHEZRON in his spare time at
home it just isn't practical for
him to put his private telephone
number on CHEZRON letters and,

faced with an avalanche of mail
each evening,he just cannot find
time to chat on the phone - he
must give priority to readers'
orders and queries.

If you were running a user group
for users of a system for which
there was little commercial
software available then received
several copies of OUTLET would
you not feel it your duty, nay,
be delighted to advise your
members in your own monthly
newsletter? Well? Have you been
advised? Is the only regular
Disciple software ever REVIEWED
in FORMAT?

Both Ron and I have many regrets
about not attending the ZXM but

it's a major upheaval for us let
alone the cost and we just can't
face it while burdened with the
daily task of producing OUTLET.

                        - Brian

I like "That's The Ticket"
because I get to play the"heavy"

Re the subscription disks - the
answer is please send them as
soon as possible after receiving

certainly not later than the
25th of the month as, after that

month-ending work in sending out

                     - RON

From Brian to Nick Lewis

Regarding your request for ideas
in this month's OUTCLASS, Nick,
I'd be interested in a routine
to PRINT a value on screen.I may
never need to do this because I
doubt that I would ever write a
routine to crunch numbers faster
than the ROM routines so I would
probably always use BASIC where,
for example, there is a user
INPUT, followed by a calculation
and then the answer displayed.
Nevertheless, I'm curious as to
how it's done because, although
I CAN work out methods of doing
it,they would actually be longer
than the calculation! I assume
there must be some simple way of
doing it?
                  - Brian

From: H.J. Curley,  RHYL


Dear Ron & Brian,

On upgrading from a ZX printer
to a Kempston E interface and a
Brother M-1009 printer, OUTLET
text does not line feed at the
end of a page and the beginning
of the next page.


There does not seem to be a
fault in the interface or
printer because TASWORD, ARTIST
II and the ANIMATOR all work
perfectly. Any help would be
appreciated.

To H.J. Curley from Brian

You will also see that no line
space is left between paragraphs
on your OUTLET print-outs
although they appear on-screen.

Your own letter, presumably
typed on Tasword is the same so
it may be worth your looking at
Page 4 of your printer manual
and altering dipswitch 2-7 which
will send a line feed at the end
of each line. I know the dip-
switches are very awkward to get
at on the M1009 but it may solve
your problem. Re-check that the
other programs you mentioned
still work o.k. If not,alter the
dipswitch back or I think you
can customise Tasword instead.

I'm reviewing all the print
routines in OUTLET so there may
be future changes. However, as
an experiment, I've made an
immediate change to the text
mode print-outs to send 32
spaces at the end of each page
instead of a line feed. This
should force your printer to
print one blank line. Try it now
before altering your dipswitch!

Please write again if you still
get problems. Anyone else with
print-out problems should also
write in. However, it may be
impossible to satisfy everyone
as there are so many systems all
set-up in different ways and
many OUTLET programs have varied
print routines so we may have to
compromise.            - Brian

From Andrew Clapham, Nottingham.


Dear Outlet Subscribers,

I hadn't realised until I saw
the last editorial,just how much
of a commitment Ron and Brian
had made to producing Outlet.
It's obvious that to maintain
such a consistently high
standard takes up a tremendous
amount of time. Well I may be
seeing it wrongly but it seems
that if the readership does not
grow to a point where it becomes
financially viable then there is
some risk of it folding. I for
one don't want that to happen.
As an early subscriber I have
thoroughly enjoyed each issue.

It occurred to me that the best
way to thank Ron and Brian (and
of course their long-suffering
families)for all their time
invested on our behalf is to do
something to spread the word.
Outlet deserves a much larger
readership. So if you, Ron and
Brian could provide me and any-
one else with an A4 sheet made
up of 6 adverts for Outlet say,
we can Xerox them off and cut
them up as handouts. Here in
Nottingham, I know of computer
shops that might be suitable for
asking if they will take some
for customers to pick up and in
addition we have a microcomputer
club who might take some or
include an insert in their News-
letter.

Another possibility might be to
give one's kids some to take to
their schools to give to their
Spectrum-owning friends or their
parents. I hope that this does
not sound like a crusade, for it
is intended to be a few suggest-
ions of ways to advertise with-
out spending a lot of money. You
may have more ideas to add to
the list.
         Happy New Year!
               Andrew Clapham.

Many thanks, Andrew - and also
for your letter to New Computer
Express! We do have a standard,
promotional letter and will send
you (and anyone else on request)
a few master copies. We are
extremely grateful for any help!
                  - Ron & Brian

From Andrew Clapham, Nottingham

Dear Ron and Brian,

After looking at my growing
collection of carts devoted to
Outlet,I have decided that I
must do some pruning eventually,
after all, what will it be like
in a year's time? Then I thought
about how it is for new
subscribers. It will be only the
most avid who will purchase all
the back issues.

So how do the part-work special-
ists deal with it? Answer:
spin-offs. So how about a series
of compilation carts/disks on
specific themes taken from the
material from back issues,inter-
spersed with some of the famous

Outlaughs (humour) to make for
variety.

It may help if you were to start
advertising compilations, along
with the usual monthly, later in
the year, of say, tech tips and
beginners' material - perhaps
Outclasses deserve a disk on
their own.

How about trying MGT to see if
they would include an Outlet
Flyer along with their advert-
ising for the Plus D and
Disciple and, for that matter,
Applied Technology and E.E.C.
Ltd. suppliers of IF1 and micro-
drives. After all its an induce-
ment to buy the product.
                - Andrew Clapham

To Andrew Clapham from Brian

I have considered some sort of
spin-off from OUTLET but I was
thinking more in terms of say,
a compilation of utilities that
never got into OUTLET simply
because of shortage of room.
However, when I started such a
compilation, I finished up using
them in OUTLET eventually and my
compilation dwindled away! As
OUTLET grows we must surely get
an excess of material building
up eventually which can then be
published as "OUTLET EXTRA".

What do others think about
compiling material already used
in OUTLET, say "THE BEST OF
OUTLET UTILITIES"?

We have already written to MGT
and, despite having received an
encouraging reply, have heard
nothing more from them. As you
say, promoting software which
runs on their hardware can only
enhance their own product. Bob
Brenchley who "runs" INDUG has a
big advantage in that he does
not need to pay for adverts- MGT
inform all new purchasers of the
Disciple and Plus D about INDUG
and he does not have to pay many
postage costs (since he doesn't
bother answering letters!)

By the way, going back to your
previous letter, there's little
danger of OUTLET just "folding"
suddenly (short of a bolt of
lightning!) - the worst that

might happen is a reduction in
content and presentation and,
perhaps, going bi-monthly or
quarterly. If I have to get a
full-time job I would run OUTLET
in my spare time. However, this
does not look likely. Although
we are struggling financially,
OUTLET continues to grow, albeit
very slowly!
                      - Brian.

> Trevor Wright, Melton Mowbray,

Dear Ron,

Bob Brenchley who runs INDUG
does seem to have rather a back-
log of mail! I've written a
couple of letters, to which I
have had no reply. He cries out
for letters but then doesn't
print them!

Now to answer some of your
queries about INDUG. 1.Yes there
is a newsletter in A5 booklet
style which arrives every month
if you pay your dues of `10 per
year. 2. I have had no contact
with other members either
through the letters page or any
other method. (See comment in

first paragraph) 3. I will do my
best to contact him to plug
OUTLET 4. I enclose an appli-
cation form to join INDUG which
comes out of the introductory
copy of 'FORMAT', the news-
letter. I sent it off and have
been receiving a mailing ever
since.

Going back to the newsletter
'FORMAT', it is a very well
produced booklet produced on a
DTP system. It has various
articles on general computing
interest e.g. MIDI, adventuring,
as well as programs to type in,
letters page(!), news page etc.
It also produces some software
which it sells on tape for `3.95
each. I haven't yet bought any.

Here are some of them:- IBU -
backs up discs if you only have
one drive ART STUDIO - converts
to disc operation G-HACKER -
graphic investigator for
commercial programs TASCON -
conversion program for Tasword
128 and Tasword+2 PLUS D HACKER
- lets you examine commercial
programs.

The IBU I can recommend as I
typed it in from the newsletter.

Hope this will fill a few gaps.

Yours,

Trevor Wright.

To: Trevor Wright from Ron

Dear Trevor,

Many thanks for your letter and
information on INDUG. From this,
and actual sample copies of the
FORMAT magazine received from
other readers, I now have a
clearer picture of what INDUG is
all about. The first thing I
found out is that I should have
received an application form to
join INDUG when I purchased my
Disciple from Rockfort. This was
not received which was a pity
because I reckon I would have
been better submitting an
anonymous application rather
than writing wearing my CHEZRON
hat.

However, I am writing again to
Bob Brenchley with a straight -
forward application to join,
together with my ten quid and
wait to see what happens this
time.
                          - RON

From Harold Burton, EDINBURGH

Dear Ron and Brian

Many thanks for back issues and
the current disc. How was it
that I did not discover OUTLET
sooner? [perhaps your "user"
group doesn't think it worth
mentioning?- BC]

What a wealth of knowledge is
there for me to digest now that
there is no other source of
serious programs for the
Spectrum. Getting a Disciple and
disc drive was one revolution,
discovering OUTLET is certainly
another!

I  would  like  to  make  a  few

comments  on  points  from   the
letters and editorial pages.

I have been a member of INDUG
since the early days. It has a
monthly mag. devoted mainly to
use of the Disciple and Plus D,
help and letter pages, news and
any modifications to the
Disciple systems file of which
there have been several. It is
run by Bob Brenchley who I think
prefers to deal with queries on
his HOTLINE phone instead of by
letter.

Regarding the speed of the key
press, I agree that often the
repeat is too slow. The worst
example of this is in the
TASWORD program which I am using

now since that is how you would
like letters to be sent. I much
prefer SPECTRAL WRITER by Softek
which was given free with the
WAFADRIVE originally. This has
many features which are better
than TASWORD and I have modified
it with the update and my own
features to suit the Disciple
and disc drive. The speed of the
cursor alone is a worthwhile
feature compared with the
maddeningly slow one of TASWORD.
The only drawback to S/WRITER is
the inability to set the right-
hand margin which is the reason
I am using TASWORD now!If anyone
knows how to modify Spectral
Writer further to do 32 columns
I would be pleased to know. Also
I would be willing to give
details of my mods.

Regarding keyboards,I have found
that the Dk'tronics one is the
best.This is the view of one who
is a touch-typist and is accust-
omed to a normal type keyboard,
not one with a lot of extra keys
which add to the confusion. Also
it is easily modified to
accommodate peripherals such as
Disciple. The base can be
removed and the very strong top
used alone above the extra item.
Also I have modified the keypad
to include a one-keypress comma,
which is very useful when typing
DATA statements.

Yours sincerely

HAROLD BURTON

To Harold Burton from Brian


Thanks. Yes, I'm a touch-typist
too - using the Fuller keyboard.
If you see one for sale second-
hand try and get it - it has a
full-stop, comma and space-bar,
all in the correct (typewriter)
places plus one-key DELETE and
one-key EXTENDED MODE and SHIFT
EXTENDED MODE. The only weakness
when programming is that there's
a built-in (it contains its own
microchip circuitry)delay of one
or two seconds on the SHIFT-
EXTENDED MODE key to allow time
for one-finger typists to find
the subsequent key and this is
much too slow for touch-typing.

Try POKE 23561,10 : POKE 23562,3
in Tasword's start line to speed
it up(end of line is still tacky
though).
                      - Brian

From David Wornham,  Worcs.

Dear Brian,

Thanks for reviewing "Flexipage"
in edition 13 of Outlet. This
early edition has since had many
improvements, and the latest has
benefitted more from your
comments.

The instruction booklet has now
been re-written to expand on
detail and has added "planner"
sheets and a"step by step" exer-
cise development booklet with
the advice of Grampian Regional
Council where Spectrums are used
in schools.

The program improvements include


a fast display speed which is
virtually "instant", "help"
pages,logical order of UDGs etc.

I note your comments that Outlet
is not large enough to attract
free review copies, so am trying
to help! I am a "one man band"
who cannot justify more than the
occasional small advertisement,
so must rely on reviews, and now
enclose an update. I do appreci-
ate the time necessary to review
a program with a wide variation
of use such as "Flexipage" but
do request, in accordance with
your wish to provide "in-depth
info", that you mention other
features of Flexipage previously
omitted from your review, namely
the automatic scoring and print-

out options in the interactive
mode and the flexibility of Disk
(Microdrive)/Tape/Memory trans-
fer of programs and data.

The one demo. page you selected
only showed the half screen
option, so your subscribers may
not realize the potential to
display "full" (10 lines of
double height) screen displays.

Your query on the large letter-
ing is clarified by saying that
although all pages are displayed
at double height, larger letters
can be made up from the user
defined graphics.

Full details of "Flexipage" will
be sent to anyone sending a

stamped, addressed envelope, but
I enclose a free "demo" for use
in Outlet if you have room.

          Yours sincerely ,

             David Wornham
             20 The Parklands
             Droitwich Spa
             Worcs. WR9 7DG

P.S. FLEXIPAGE 200,complete with
graphics designer, is available
on Opus Discovery or +3 disk at
`12.50 or tape at `10.50.

BOTH LESS 10% FOR OUTLET READERS

[Should be no problem transferr-
ing to microdrive or Disciple/+D
either - BC]

To David Wornham from Brian

First, let me apologize for the
delay in publish your OUTLETTER.
It should have appeared last
month but somehow we temporarily
misplaced your disk in the Xmas
rush...

We'll certainly put your demo
program in a future issue of
OUTLET and I'll add a few words
somewhere then about the various
improvements. For the moment, I
must agree, after a quick look,
that the graphics are very much
faster, the explanation of the
on-screen prompts makes things
clearer and the manuals look
very good. Ye gods! - you have
put a lot of effort into this!
                         - Brian.

Dear Ron & Brian,
